claims.text: The target MPEA is brittle at room temperature, has low tensile ductility and moderate yield strength, and likely has a BCC or BCC/FCC structure.
Hot rolling near 1200 °C followed by 75% cold rolling, annealing at 900 °C for 5 min, and aging at 650 °C for 20 h is an effective stepwise processing sequence.
The proposed stepwise treatment will create two coherent precipitate populations consisting of δ lamellae and γ″ particles.
The hot-rolling stage induces deformation and texture.
Cold rolling introduces a high dislocation density and nucleation sites for subsequent precipitation.
A 900 °C, 5 min anneal forms metastable coherent δ-phase lamellae.
A 650 °C, 20 h aging treatment forms fine coherent γ″ particles.
The δ precipitates have a D0a structure, a width of about 40 nm, and a length of 0.5–1 μm.
The γ″ precipitates have a D022 structure and an approximately 10 nm spheroidal morphology.
Both precipitate populations are rich in Ni, Fe, Ta, and W and maintain coherent interfaces with the matrix.
The δ lamellae strengthen the alloy, store dislocations, and can be sheared by slip bands without cracking.
The γ″ particles strengthen the alloy through order hardening and lattice-misfit strengthening.
Small precipitate size and low lattice misfit prevent crack initiation at γ″-matrix interfaces.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission, relieve stress concentrations, and prevent premature crack initiation.
The dual-precipitate structure supplies approximately 1 GPa of additional strength while maintaining high strain hardening and ductility.
The processed alloy will attain a room-temperature UTS of approximately 2.0–2.2 GPa and tensile elongation of at least 15%.
The treatment will increase yield strength from approximately 600 MPa in the as-cast state to approximately 1.4–2.0 GPa.
The processed alloy will retain yield strength above 1.0 GPa at 800 °C because the coherent precipitates are thermally stable.
The baseline as-cast or conventionally processed MPEA has approximately 600 MPa yield strength and less than 5% tensile ductility.
The strategy is applicable mainly to MPEAs capable of forming low-misfit coherent precipitates and may fail when precipitates are incoherent or unstable at the aging temperature.
